title: Free-set marginal of a Bernoulli restriction
statement:
Fix $n \in \bbn$, a real parameter $p$, and a subset $T \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ of the coordinates. Draw a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on $n$ variables, and write $J$ for its set of free variables (the coordinates $\rho$ leaves unset). Then the probability that every coordinate of $T$ is left free is
\[
  \Pr\bigl[\,T \subseteq J\,\bigr] \;=\; p^{\abs{T}},
\]
that is, the total Bernoulli weight of those restrictions whose free variables include $T$ equals $p^{\abs{T}}$.
hypotheses_covered: subset T of the n coordinates
event that T is contained in the free variables of the restriction
replaced:
Under a Bernoulli($p$)-random restriction with free-coordinate set $J$, the probability that a
fixed set $T$ is contained in $J$ is
\[
  \Pr[T \subseteq J] \;=\; p^{\abs{T}} .
\]
This is the first-moment half of O'Donnell Proposition 4.17.
